sections.name: In an emergency
sections.title: What to do in a dental emergency.
sections.text: Over-the-counter pain relief such as ibuprofen or paracetamol can help while you wait, but don’t apply aspirin directly to the gum. If swelling is spreading to your face, jaw or neck, seek urgent medical attention.

card.title: Knocked-out tooth?
card.text: Handle the tooth by the crown only, not the root. If it is clean, try to place it back in the socket or store it in milk, and get to us as quickly as possible.

items: How quickly can I be seen for a dental emergency?
Get in touch and we will arrange an appointment as quickly as possible. Weekend and out-of-hours appointments are also available.
How much is an emergency appointment?
Emergency appointments are £50, including X-rays. Weekend and out-of-hours appointments are £200, including treatment. You get a written plan with prices before any follow-up treatment begins.
What counts as a dental emergency?
Significant pain, swelling, injury or the sudden loss of a filling or crown that is affecting your ability to eat or function. If you’re unsure, get in touch and we’ll advise you.
Do I need to be a registered patient?
No. You do not need to be an existing patient to have an emergency appointment at Concept Dental.
Will I need follow-up treatment?

In most cases, yes. Emergency appointments focus on resolving the immediate problem, and definitive treatment is usually carried out at a follow-up appointment with costs confirmed in writing beforehand.
